title: Cabo Verde agricultural country profile evidence
purpose: Record official agricultural survey and statistics sources, crop and livestock observations, dated retail-market evidence and unresolved farm-budget inputs. This is a research evidence file only and is not an activated calculator profile.

sources.note: The ministry states that its agricultural statistics directorate collects, produces, organizes and disseminates agricultural data. The page currently says statistical data will be made available soon; it is a source lead, not a numerical dataset.

quality_notes: The yearbook says MAA estimates horticultural production using information about quantities of seeds sold during the year. These figures must not be presented as measured harvested quantities or used to calculate yields without matching area and methodology.
The 2022/23 rainfed campaign runs from May to April of the following year. Do not treat it as a calendar-year observation.
The yearbook contains national production totals but the cited crop tables do not provide compatible harvested-area denominators, crop-cut yields, or farm-level yield distributions.

The yearbook's prose gives a total meat production figure in tonnes, while Table 8.6 is explicitly labelled in kilograms and the species values sum to approximately 3.93 million kg. Preserve the table's stated kg unit and flag the prose unit as an apparent reporting error.

sources.title: GIEWS Country Brief — The Republic of Cabo Verde
sources.publisher: FAO Global Information and Early Warning System

observations.status: FAO reports the official estimate at about 3,600 tonnes, nearly 80 percent above the low five-year average; still an estimate, with no matching harvested-area denominator in the brief.
Preliminary estimate, nearly 40 percent below the already low five-year average; do not treat as a final census result.

quality_notes: FAO's November 2024 forecast for 2024 maize was 1,444 tonnes; later briefs revised the estimate to about 3,600 tonnes. Preserve the forecast/estimate chronology and do not combine them as separate final observations.
FAO attributes the 2025 decline to erratic and below-average rainfall, drought during crop development, reduced planted area, high labour costs and abandonment of some agricultural activity.
FAO reports locally produced maize retail prices rose by up to 5 percent between October and December 2025; this is a price movement, not an absolute price or a farm-gate quotation.

sources.title: VI Recenseamento Geral da Agricultura (RGA 2025)
sources.publisher: Government of Cabo Verde, Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, and INE
sources.note: The government launched the sixth general agricultural census in July 2025. The official resolution provides for implementation during 2025 and 2026. A later ministry recruitment notice sought enumerators available January-March 2026. As of this research date, the final national tables or downloadable census dataset have not been located; request the latest RGA results and preserve the differing implementation notices.

sources.title: FAO Agricultural Integrated Survey Programme (AGRISurvey) — Cabo Verde
sources.publisher: FAO, in collaboration with INE and MAA
sources.note: FAO reports support for annual agricultural surveys, with a 2024 farm income, labour and productivity module and a 2025 production methods and environment module. The holding-listing operation was completed in the first half of 2024. FAO notes that Cabo Verde did not previously have regular agricultural surveys and that the programme is establishing an annual system.

sources.title: Observatório do Mercado
sources.publisher: Ministério de Agricultura e Ambiente, Cabo Verde
sources.note: The ministry says the observatory monitors stocks and price evolution for maize, rice, wheat, wheat flour, beans, oil, sugar and milk nationally and internationally. The accessible page describes the service but does not expose a dated numerical price series.

sources.title: VI Recenseamento Geral da Agricultura — Resolution 88/2025
sources.note: The resolution establishes the VI General Agricultural Census for implementation across the national territory during 2025 and 2026. It confirms the 2015 RGA as the last completed census at the time of the resolution. Final 2025/2026 numeric results were not located in this review.

sources.title: 2026 Programme of Incentives for Protected Cultivation — Agricultural Greenhouses
sources.note: The programme provides a 75% subsidy for eligible greenhouse materials and installation, subject to a maximum subsidy of CVE 900,000 per farmer. This is a public support ceiling, not a market quotation, actual farmer cost, unit greenhouse cost or general input-price observation. It may be used only as policy context until actual invoices/quotations are collected.

sources.title: FAO AGRISurvey — Cabo Verde annual agricultural survey programme
sources.note: FAO reports 2024 rotating module on farm income, labour and productivity (ILP), 2025 module on production methods and environment (PME), and completion of the agricultural holdings listing in the first half of 2024. Public microdata or full tabulations still need to be checked; programme description alone is not extracted observations.

sources.title: Government investment in the 2025/2026 rainfed agricultural campaign
sources.publisher: Government of Cabo Verde, Ministry of Agriculture and Environment

observations.status: Government announced total investment of CVE 44.5 million for strengthening the 2025/26 rainfed campaign.
Government programme planned subsidized seeds and planting materials.
Programme supply items; no farmer unit price or quantity schedule exposed in the announcement.
Programme planned extension support in all municipalities and pest control support, including trained applicators and biological phytosanitary products.

quality_notes: CVE 44.5 million is a national programme budget, not a per-hectare production cost or a farmer-paid price.
The announcement does not provide unit prices, beneficiary allocations, quantities, crop-specific seed rates or out-of-pocket farmer contributions.
Do not use this programme total in the profit calculator as a cost input.

sources.title: VI General Agricultural Census legal mandate and scope
sources.publisher: Boletim Oficial, Government of Cabo Verde, Resolution 88/2025
sources.note: The resolution mandates the sixth General Agricultural Census across Cabo Verde during 2025 and 2026, covering all family and non-family agricultural and agro-pastoral holdings. The previous completed census was in 2015. This establishes the census scope but is not a numeric dataset.

extraction_status: Batch 40 adds the Government's 2025/26 rainfed campaign support programme: CVE 44.5 million national investment for subsidized seeds, vegetative planting materials and technical assistance. This is programme-level funding, not a unit cost or farmer-paid input quotation. The VI RGA 2025/2026 legal mandate remains active, but final census tables and municipality-level crop yields have not been located. FAO's January 2026 estimate of about 1,100 tonnes maize production in 2025 remains preliminary and lacks matching harvested-area data. Retail price movements are not farm-gate prices. Cabo Verde remains directory-only.

publication_decision.reason: Do not activate Cabo Verde from aggregate or seed-sales-based production estimates, a single-city retail snapshot, or incomplete census evidence. The 2025 maize estimate is preliminary and lacks a compatible area denominator; the VI RGA 2025/2026 final results were not located. The 2026 greenhouse subsidy is a support ceiling, not a cost quotation.
publication_decision.protected_scope: No existing country profile, commodity profile, calculator formula, calculation or production deployment is changed by this research entry.

administrative_geography.source_note: INE's official 2021 Population and Housing Census GIS service provides a CONCELHOS feature layer with the Concelho field.
